answer: Time can't be cloned. Each tide the network mints one opal seed, and a ballot needs a quartz chain: one hour of sequential grinding from the seed, each vertex hashed from the last, chained to the prior tide's output — like Chia's timelords, who hold ten-minute blocks with VDFs no parallel farm can rush. GPU-farm sybils die by the quartz check: no answer before 60 minutes, yet every honest crystal verifies in 40 ms. Forging 10,000 ballots burns 10,000 hours of rented silicon, $12,000 in GPU time, plus $20 locked per vertex. One short chain, and the whole fleet of paper clocks stops dead.
